_comment: The 17 KWP adaptation channels, the ff_fuel E% store, and the stock
adaptation-reset flag (issue #47 / #38 / #26/#28, brief H2, 2026-09-24).
WHY: a stock, tester-free path `fault_clear_then_adaptation_reset`
0x0D1068 (a 100 ms task process) resets ALL 17 adaptation channels to
their block-8 defaults -- the fuel trims 4/8/10 among them -- on the
first application boot when 0x7FEB59 != 0 AND bit 0 of 0x7FA02B (EEP_CONF
block 11 mirror +11) is set.  The OBD download itself does NOT set the
bit; the tester's routine 0xC5 (31 C5 / 33 C5, the immobiliser /
component-protection adaptation step) does, raw-writing EEPROM 0x28B/0x2AB
(re/findings/eeprom.md section 11, setter 0x087494).  A plain 14 FF 00 DTC
clear does NOT reset the channels (0x038D64 has one caller, behind both
gates).  The ff_fuel E% store at block 8 +19 survives the reset; the old
+2 did not.
RUN THIS BEFORE AND AFTER EVERY FLASH AND AFTER EVERY DTC CLEAR, so that
a reset is visible: read once, do the flash / clear, read again, diff.
A changed channel block after a flash means the tool ran routine 0xC5;
a changed +19 (E% store) means something other than the adaptation reset
touched it.  On the bus, also note whether 31 C5 / 33 C5 was sent.
python3 logging/med9log.py log --session \
logging/sessions/adaptation_channels.json \
--bus gs_usb:0 --seconds 20 -o logs/2026-xx-xx_adaptation.csv
All cells are the application RAM the DDLI route reads (session 0x89).
The channel RAM 0x7FD062-0x7FD06D and the block-8 mirror 0x7F9F80-0x7F9F9F
are the same values two ways: the block-8 mirror payload +(k+1) is
channel k, and 0x038D64/adaptation_restore_all move both together.
Ranges verified end to end in tests/test_adaptation_reset_path.py
(VERIFIED-DYNAMIC, emulated).
Channel map (F4/G7, re/symbols.csv; block 8 payload +(k+1)):
ch1  0x7FD06B (+2, clamped 0/0)   ch4  0x7FD065 (+5, mixture)
ch8  0x7FD067 (+9, ksta)          ch10 0x7FD066 (+11, fgru)
ch13 0x7FD062 (+14)               ch7  is the only tester-writable one
on this dataset (access words 0x40).
The E% store is block 8 payload +19 = mirror 0x7F9F93.

vars.name: adaptation_channels_ram
vars.notes: the 12 implemented adaptation-channel RAM cells; each byte 128 = 1.0 (Q7) for the multiplier channels; reset to defaults by 0x038D64

vars.name: adap_ch4_mixture
vars.notes: channel 4, running mixture Q7 multiplier, limits 64..141, default 128; a fuel trim (docs/05 3.3)

vars.name: adap_ch10_fgru
vars.notes: channel 10, fgru_trim input, limits 26..179, default 128; a fuel trim

vars.name: adap_ch8_ksta
vars.notes: channel 8, start-quantity ksta Q7 multiplier, limits 64..141, default 128; a fuel trim

vars.name: adap_ch1
vars.notes: channel 1 = block 8 payload +2; its only reader clamps it to 0/0; this is where E4's +2 E% store wrongly landed

vars.name: adap_ch13
vars.notes: channel 13 = block 8 payload +14, the one constant-offset client eeprom_map --clients saw

vars.name: blk8_mirror
vars.notes: the EEP_CONF block-8 RAM mirror: +0/+1 {id,ver} stamp, +2..+18 the 17 channels, +19 the ff_fuel E% store, +29 the manager ReplV, +30/+31 checksum

vars.name: blk8_e_pct_store
vars.notes: block 8 payload +19: the ff_fuel ethanol-percent store; SURVIVES the adaptation reset (proved emulated)

vars.name: adaptation_reset_flag
vars.notes: EEP_CONF block 11 mirror +11; BIT 0 = adaptation-reset request. Loaded from EEPROM 0x28B at start-up. Set by routine 0xC5 (0x087494), cleared by 0x0D1068. Expect 0 on a normally-running ECU

vars.name: abnormal_boot_latch
vars.notes: gate 1 of 0x0D1068; 1 if this boot follows a programming request (magic 0x7F8020) or the flashed HW/SW identity mismatches. Distinct from G5's 0x7FEB65 engine-running gate
